# claude-harness

Multi-agent harness for long-running application development. Based on [Anthropic's harness design pattern](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/harness-design-long-running-apps).

## What it does

Orchestrates three specialized agents in a Plan-Build-Evaluate loop:

- **Planner** — expands a brief into a product spec (high-level, no implementation details)
- **Generator** — builds the application in a continuous session
- **Evaluator** — tests the running app like a real user, produces pass/fail verdicts

Each agent runs in a fresh context with file-based handoffs (`.harness/*.md`). The separation of generator and evaluator — inspired by GANs — produces dramatically better results than solo generation.

## Skills

| Skill | Usage | Purpose |
|-------|-------|---------|
| `/harness` | `/harness "build a retro game maker"` | Full Plan-Build-Evaluate loop |
| `/harness-eval` | `/harness-eval` | Standalone evaluation against spec |
| `/harness-status` | `/harness-status` | Inspect current harness state |
| `/harness-simplify` | `/harness-simplify evaluator` | Test if a component is still needed |

## Agents

| Agent | Model | Triggers on |
|-------|-------|-------------|
| `harness-planner` | opus | Dispatched by /harness for spec creation |
| `harness-generator` | opus | Dispatched by /harness for implementation |
| `harness-evaluator` | opus | Dispatched by /harness or /harness-eval for QA |

## Hooks

| Event | What it does |
|-------|-------------|
| `SessionStart` | Loads `.harness/state.json` into context for resumption |

## How it works

```
/harness "build X"
  │
  ├── Phase 1: Initialize .harness/ workspace
  │
  ├── Phase 2: Planner agent → spec.md
  │   └── User approves spec before continuing
  │
  ├── Phase 3: Build-Evaluate loop (up to 5 rounds)
  │   ├── Generator agent → builds app (worktree isolation)
  │   ├── Evaluator agent → tests app → eval-report.md
  │   └── Verdict: PASS (done) / ITERATE (next round) / PIVOT (restart)
  │
  └── Phase 4: Finalize
```

User confirmation required at: spec approval, each eval round, pivot decisions.

## Progressive simplification

Every component encodes an assumption about what the model can't do alone. As models improve, some components become unnecessary overhead.

`/harness-simplify` removes one component at a time and compares quality. If quality holds, the component gets disabled in `config.json`. The harness adapts to the model it runs on.

## File structure

```
.harness/                    # Created per-project by /harness
├── config.json              # Component toggles, model selection
├── state.json               # Current phase and round
├── spec.md                  # Planner output
├── build-summary-N.md       # Generator output per round
├── eval-report-N.md         # Evaluator output per round
└── simplification-log.md    # /harness-simplify results
```

## Installation

```bash
# Already in ~/.claude/plugins/claude-harness/
# Enable in Claude Code settings or use:
cc --plugin-dir ~/.claude/plugins/claude-harness
```

## Cost expectations

Based on Anthropic's published benchmarks with Opus 4.6:

| Configuration | Typical cost | Typical time |
|---|---|---|
| Full harness (3 rounds) | ~$125 | ~4 hours |
| Single round (no iteration) | ~$75 | ~2.5 hours |
| Without evaluator | ~$70 | ~2 hours |
| Solo (no harness) | ~$9 | ~20 min |

The solo approach is 20x cheaper but produces broken, incomplete applications. The harness trades cost for quality.
